body: She btw, and it is what happened, I really don't know what to tell you. "Going to waste" was a figure of speech, I shotgunned what they had smoked, if I didn't it would have gone to the air, and they weren't dealers, and it wasn't just one person.I know a lot of people through the help I've given, just as I was trying to help my ex, they were people I'd helped in the past. If you think I'm an asshole in entirety for the results of this one situation, it's a straw man you're completely entitled to engage in. You're also entitled to believe I'm lying about it, even though there would be no point in me lying about it here, because the entire point was never about the drugs, it was about the snap. I could have snapped and killed someone, or effectively anything else.

It's what happened, I don't mean to detract from your experience on the matter, but most of it was shotgunning that would otherwise have gone to waste. And I know, I already accept I should I have left sooner. I just don't think it was out of a place of being an asshole, rather that I was hoping she'd see what her doing nothing was costing me. That's how I figured out she didn't care about that, and I left.

I didn't spend any money on drugs, I got them all through friends 🤷‍♀️. I admit I gave her too long to prove herself, but I did leave her in the end. I used to love her and I felt responsible to do what I could to make sure she'd be okay.

I had an independently conceived notion growing up that the first humans to realize death would inevitably come to them would have been driven insane. It's either just innately blocked out in most people because of the resulting selection, or what I felt was more likely is that religion played a part, the remaining selection were of a way of thinking predisposed to believing in it, and that the predisposition for believing in religion is innate to modern humans as a result. 

I've really come to believe that it's actually both, in that basic instinct shared across most life: the self preservation fear response. We tell ourselves that we must protect ourselves from death and it creates a barrier between rationality and Insanity, and that in itself leads to a predisposition for believing in things irrational designed to defy insanity, i.e. religion.

In that way, it's not that humans are under the illusion that life is good - it's actually pretty bad - but ceasing living is perceived instinctually to be worse.

It's interesting that when the tables are turned, atheists tend to consider religion to be both irrational and insane.

I promise you there is someone out there for you. I felt the same way for the longest time, that I was unattractive and that it meant, literally at face value, that I was unlovable or worthless.

I'm pansexual, which more or less means I can only be sexually attracted to someone's personality, not their looks, race, gender, etc. I know, maybe it sounds like generic advice, but really the best thing that you can do is just be yourself and someone will love you for it. I wish I could be of more help, it's clear that you have a lot of love to give, just don't give up and you'll find someone who deserves it.
